The initiative integrates facial recognition and fingerprint data directly with national criminal justice databases to create a continuous surveillance register. While framed as child protection, civil liberties advocates warn the centralized biometric architecture creates severe privacy risks across an already vulnerable public sector IT estate.

Vesti kertoi myöhemmin Komsomolskaja Pravdan sotakirjeenvaihtajan Aleksandr Kotsin näkemyksestä. Kotsin mukaan lennokki-isku olisi ollut harjoitus Kaliningradin mahdollista saartoa varten. articles.title: Native Go Extensions Bypass Legacy PostgreSQL C Dependency Bottlenecks
articles.content: PostgreSQL extensions in Go gopgext builds PostgreSQL extensions from plain Go code, using TinyGo. Mark a function with //gopgext:function and it becomes a SQL function: gopgext writes the C glue, the install script and the control file. Get started Documentation GitHub Experimental gopgext is experimental. Don’t use it in production: a bug in the generated code or the Go runtime runs inside the server, where it can crash it or corrupt data, and the API and generated SQL may change without notice. Just Go A project is plain Go files. The standard library works: fmt , regexp , encoding/json , crypto/* , maps, generics, iterators, defer / recover . Types map to SQL Strings, numbers, arrays, NULL s, sets, rows, timestamps, UUIDs and JSON map to SQL types. Define your own data types and composite types in Go. Queries and errors Run SQL through SPI, return errors with SQLSTATE codes, log, read settings and stay responsive to query cancellation. Beyond functions Write triggers, aggregates, GiST, GIN, SP-GiST and BRIN operator classes, index access methods, foreign data wrappers and query hooks. Proven on contrib Ports of PostgreSQL’s contrib modules ( pgcrypto , hstore , pg_stat_statements , cube , …) pass upstream’s regression tests. Safe coexistence Several Go extensions load in one backend. PostgreSQL errors never unwind through Go frames, and results are copied into PostgreSQL memory. Hello, world # package main import ( "strings" "gopgext/pg" ) // Hello returns a greeting for name. // //gopgext:function immutable parallel=safe func Hello ( name string ) string { return "Hello, " + name + "!" } // Shout upper-cases s. An empty string raises an error. // //gopgext:function immutable parallel=safe func Shout ( s string ) ( string , error ) { if s == "" { return "" , pg . Errorf ( pg . CodeInvalidParameterValue , "nothing to shout" ) } return strings . ToUpper ( s ) + "!" , nil } func main () {} // runs once per backend, when PostgreSQL loads the library gopgext init hello # creates hello/go.mod and hello/main.go gopgext install hello # builds hello.so, hello.control, hello--1.0.sql and installs them psql -c 'CREATE EXTENSION hello' -c "SELECT hello('world')" # hello # --------------- # Hello, world! The tutorial walks through it step by step. A sibling project # gopgext uses the same approach as gokm , which builds Linux kernel modules from Go: a custom TinyGo target and runtime layer for the host, a C runtime compiled by the host’s own build system (PGXS here, kbuild there), and generated glue.

articles.title: Zero C# Strips Garbage Collection for Native Systems Programming
articles.summary: The Zero C# compiler project has successfully stripped the .NET virtual machine, runtime overhead, and garbage collector to run C# code directly on bare silicon. The architecture compiles C# syntax into standalone, native machine code with zero external dependencies, targeting embedded systems, operating system kernels, and game engines. By proving modern high-level syntax can achieve C++ performance without runtime baggage, the project challenges Rust's hegemony over modern systems programming.
articles.deck: Open-source compiler eliminates runtime dependencies to position managed C# against Rust and C++.
bullets: Systems developer released Zero C# on March 29, compiling C# directly to native machine binaries without .NET runtime libraries.
The compiler enforces manual memory management and compile-time stack allocation, eliminating garbage collection pauses entirely.
Compiled binaries measure less than 15 kilobytes, enabling direct execution on microcontrollers and embedded automotive microprocessors.
The project reached the top of developer platforms as engineers tested execution speeds against identical Rust and C++ implementations.
Embedded robotics designers began testing the compiler for deterministic real-time control systems where garbage collection spikes are fatal.
articles.why_matters: If you write C#, you can now build bare-metal microcontrollers and operating system kernels without learning Rust or C++. Eliminating garbage collection delivers zero-latency determinism, vital for autonomous vehicle sensors, industrial robotics, and aerospace control systems. Binary sizes shrink by 98% compared to standard .NET outputs, cutting cloud container cold-start delays across edge serverless functions. Software teams can reuse existing enterprise C# talent to build high-performance infrastructure code, bypassing the expensive Rust learning curve. The compiler demonstrates that runtime-heavy managed languages can be retrofitted for ultra-efficient, low-power green computing hardware environments.
